clue.text: Have a tantrum or what?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: lose your temper in a childish fit
setter's reading: the two words, shaken about, become the first part of the phrase, and the rest of the phrase names that shaking

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is having a tantrum or something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer carries its own instruction: make OR WHAT wobbly and you get THROW A, so the phrase's last word is the signal for its first two. The question mark flags this back-to-front trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a wobbly is informal British slang for losing your temper in a childish fit.

clue.text: After claret's drunk European displays intolerable sentimentality

indicators.note: a drunk person is in a jumbled state, so the wine's letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European who has had a lot of red wine becomes unbearably mawkish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the jumbled wine comes first and the E goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is used figuratively for cloying, sickly sweet emotion, like the sticky syrup.

clue.text: A recession can end in nation falling apart, survey's revealed

indicators.note: something falling apart loses its order, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of nation

explanation.surface: A report finds that an economic downturn could make a country collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconnaissance is an exploratory inspection of an area, especially a military one, which is a kind of survey.

clue.text: General knowledge's core to which old fellow regularly contributes

indicators.note: contributing at regular intervals means slotting letters in between, one at every other position
the core of a word is its middle, so only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the middle three of the nine letters
O is the standard abbreviation for old
F is the standard abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A quiz question about general knowledge to which an elderly man is a frequent contributor.
explanation.walkthrough: O and F go in alternately between W, L and E, giving WOLFE. 'General knowledge' reads as one phrase, but 'General' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: James Wolfe was the British army general who captured Quebec from the French in 1759.

clue.text: Following game both sides surround English referee?

parts.note: whist is a card game

indicators.note: to surround something is to sit on either side of it, enclosing it

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: After a match, players from both teams crowd round an English referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places the card game first. The question mark admits the definition is playful: a referee is one who whistles, not a standard sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee blows a whistle to control play, so a whistler can whimsically describe one.

clue.text: They fly Club Class at last

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the preceding word only

parts.note: the final letter of class

explanation.surface: Passengers travelling in the premium cabin of an airline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club Class' looks like the airline cabin, but the words are split: one is a stick, the other gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats are the only mammals capable of true flight.

clue.text: Put on your Sunday best, and be quick

definitions.meaning: second meaning: hurry up, an informal command

explanation.surface: Someone is told to dress up for an occasion and hurry about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to appear well dressed and, as an informal British command, to get a move on.

clue.text: Finally disposed of most of the books in the jumble after turning up

indicators.note: turning over in a down clue means reading the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a jumble is a disordered heap, so the letters are mixed up
most of a phrase means all but its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, a run of words to be cut and mixed

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets rid of most of their old books at a jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the phrase 'the books in the' with its final E removed. A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods. 'Finally disposed of' looks like wordplay for a last letter but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the kibosh on something is an informal idiom for decisively ending or scotching it.

clue.text: Give away film's ending in newspaper article appearing in Times

indicators.note: appearing inside something means sitting within it, enclosed

parts.note: in multiplication, three times four is three by four
E.T. is the Spielberg film

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of newspaper
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper review in The Times reveals how a film ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film's ending' looks like one unit, but the film is E.T. and 'ending' belongs with newspaper. Times means BY, not the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray a secret or a person is to give them away, revealing what should stay hidden.

clue.text: Top Forty on the radio

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only spoken, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals, said as two letter names

explanation.surface: The weekly countdown of the forty best-selling records broadcast on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Forty' reads as the singles chart, but Top is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To top a rival is to surpass or outdo them, which is what it means to excel.

clue.text: Elected party does a U-turn, blocking peace offer

parts.note: an elected party is in power

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so one word goes within another

parts.note: a truce is a peace agreement

indicators.note: a U-turn sends you back the way you came, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A newly elected government reverses policy and so derails a peace proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce something, such as a bill or a proposal, is to put it forward or offer it.

clue.text: For example, Emperor Hirohito ultimately wanted to follow agreement

parts.note: acting in concert means acting in agreement

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter counts

parts.note: the final letter of Hirohito

explanation.surface: The Japanese emperor Hirohito wished to abide by a treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emperor is not Hirohito but Beethoven's Fifth Piano Concerto, nicknamed the Emperor; 'For example' marks it as one instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Piano Concerto No 5 is widely known by the nickname the Emperor, so it is an example of the genre.

clue.text: Blemish tarnished screen goddess

indicators.note: to screen something is to conceal it, so the words shield a run of letters

parts.note: the run spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A film star's reputation as a screen goddess is spoiled by a blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen goddess' reads as a film star, and Ishtar was indeed a notorious 1987 film flop, but screen is the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishtar was the Mesopotamian deity of love, fertility and war.

clue.text: One tests unknown compound within the margins of error

indicators.note: within means placed inside, enclosed by something else
the margins of a page are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of error
x is the classic unknown quantity in algebra
an amine is an organic chemical compound derived from ammonia

explanation.surface: A chemist runs tests on a mystery substance while allowing for a margin of error.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner is a person who sets or marks tests, or inspects things officially.

clue.text: I count on reform following popular Democrat's installation in office

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for Democrat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A voter relies on a popular Democrat to bring reform once sworn into office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the reworked letters after IN and D.
explanation.definitionFit: An induction is the formal ceremony of admitting someone to a post or role.

clue.text: Only just head off assets being seized by British bank

indicators.note: something seized is held tight inside a grip, so one part goes within another

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
to bank on someone is to rely on them

indicators.note: the head is the very front, taken off on its own, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of assets

explanation.surface: A British bank seizes a debtor's assets, which only just stops trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank is a verb here, as in banking on something, not a financial institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely means by the narrowest margin, scarcely, which is what only just conveys.

clue.text: Thus serious illness disrupts LA Lakers' season for a game

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: something that disrupts barges into the middle of an event, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Lakers are a Los Angeles team, so their season takes the American word for autumn
TB is tuberculosis

explanation.surface: A serious illness wrecks the Los Angeles basketball team's season.
explanation.definitionFit: Softball is a bat-and-ball game similar to baseball, played with a larger ball.

clue.text: Live on air

parts.note: re means on, concerning
side means a haughty air, as in putting on side

explanation.surface: A broadcast going out live on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live on air' sounds like broadcasting, but Live is a verb meaning dwell. Putting on side is old British slang for giving yourself airs.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to have your home there, to dwell or live.

clue.text: Runs in pursuit of one travelling by water

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to be after something is to pursue it

explanation.surface: Someone runs in chase of a person crossing by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rafter is someone who rides a raft, typically down a river through rapids.

clue.text: One's shelled out too, finally getting to stand round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to stand round something is to encircle it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: to stand is to rise to your feet

indicators.note: finally applies to each word before it, keeping only their last letters

parts.note: the last letters of out and of too

explanation.surface: Someone who has paid out a lot as well finally gets to stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelled out' looks like spending money, but 'One's shelled' is the definition and 'out' is just a source of its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoise is a slow land reptile protected by a hard domed shell.

clue.text: First off, relaxation of hostilities provides setting for new agreement

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel inside it, so one letter is enclosed
with the first gone, the opening letter is removed

parts.note: détente is an easing of tension between nations
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An easing of hostilities sets the stage for a fresh accord.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, like the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: One's out for run in country? The opposite as intended

indicators.note: one thing out for another describes swapping a letter in a word
doing the opposite flips the swap round, so the letter that was going out comes in instead

parts.note: France is the country
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A jogger heads out for a country run, but things go contrary to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, you would put I out and R in; the second sentence reverses that, so I replaces R in FRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's intended is the person they plan to marry, which is what a fiancé is.

clue.text: I disheartened clerk with bold housing project

indicators.note: a house holds things inside it, so one piece goes within another
losing heart means losing the middle, so the central letters go

parts.note: stout means brave or bold
taken as written
taken as written, before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A worker complains that a dispirited clerk and a brash colleague are running a housing scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Clerk loses its middle three letters, leaving CK. Project is a verb, meaning jut, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to protrude beyond a surface, which is to stick out.

clue.text: Boy — one that's into rock

indicators.note: being into something means sitting inside it

parts.note: a crag is a steep rock face
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lad who is a fan of rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: Craig is a common masculine given name, and boy in crosswords often means any boy's name.

clue.text: Daughter's a long time rising to challenge

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A daughter takes ages to get out of bed to face a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A dare is a challenge to do something risky or bold to prove courage.

clue.text: Dish which could be ideal with nacho, almost?

indicators.note: could be suggests a possible rearrangement, so the letters may form something new
almost means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A Mexican dish that would be just right served with tortilla chips.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of a tortilla rolled round a filling and baked in chilli sauce.

clue.text: Man captured by US security agents turned very pale

indicators.note: a captive is held inside, so one piece goes within the other
turned round means facing the other way, read backwards

parts.note: the NSA is the US National Security Agency
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man arrested by American security agents went white with fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned very pale' reads as one phrase, but turned is the reversal signal and the definition is just 'very pale'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face drained of colour, grey like ash, from shock or fear.

clue.text: In report one's information leads to collective embarrassment for MI6?

parts.note: taken as written
to tell is to report
I is the Roman numeral one
gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters, so only the first of each is kept

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A report on a spy agency's data causes widespread embarrassment for British intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: Information looks like the definition, but it supplies GEN; the definition is MI6, the British foreign spy service, with the question mark showing it is given by example.
explanation.definitionFit: MI6 is the Secret Intelligence Service, so it exemplifies intelligence in the sense of a spying organisation.
